scope.description: Whether an acknowledged commit taken on a reconstructed smaller configuration survives once a majority of the committed configuration that never held it forms leadership. Fifteen in-process cases: the thirteen previously exercised restart shapes plus a lost_entry_discard case run with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and disabled. In that case a five-voter cluster is collapsed to one voter, snapshotted, made five voters again, stopped, and its former leader restarted, acknowledged on one copy, stopped; four voters return with the flag disabled, elect twice so the second leadership is in a higher term, and only then is the holder rebuilt and every store scanned for the payload.
assumptions: Real raft instances in one process over the in-memory transports and the in-memory commit-tracking log store from the captured package; rebuilt instances are reconnected to each other in both directions.
The committed configuration has five voters while the restarted holder's snapshot metadata carries the demoted single-voter configuration, so the reconstructed quorum is one of five.
The four returning voters are rebuilt with RestoreCommittedLogs disabled on purpose, so their own configuration comes from their logs and their leadership exercises the committed configuration.

The extra election is a legal sequence: after the first returning leader is stopped the remaining three of five still form a quorum, so they elect again in a strictly higher term before the holder rejoins; the payload is searched for in every store across each store's first to last index.
excluded: Disk-backed stores, real networks, crashes of the remaining majority, membership changes after the acknowledged commit, and any claim about how a client would learn of the loss beyond the completed Apply.

basis.prefix: The new case builds a five-peer cluster with MakeClusterCustom(MakeClusterOpts{Peers: 5, Bootstrap: true, CommitTrackingLogs: true, Conf: inmemConfig with TrailingLogs 10 and RestoreCommittedLogs set per case}), demotes all four non-leader peers, applies 100 commands, takes leader.Snapshot(), promotes all four back with their addresses and applies five more entries, reads the last configuration entry, its voter count, the snapshot metadata and the tracked commit index, and emits a discard_inputs CA_EVENT. It stops every instance, rebuilds the former leader over its own stores with the case flag, waits for leadership, applies one uniquely named payload recording whether the future completed and at which index, and stops it again. It then rebuilds the four voters with the flag disabled, waits for one of them to lead, stops that leader, waits for the remaining three to elect again in a higher term, and only then rebuilds the original holder with the flag disabled and waits. It finally scans every rebuilt instance's log store for the payload and emits an entry_discard CA_EVENT with the reconstructed voter count, the acknowledgement and its index, the holder's and both returning leadership terms, how many stores still hold the payload, whether the holder still holds it, the holder's last log index after the rejoin, and the derived durable_on_majority and discarded flags.
basis.responsibility: NewRaft owns the reconstruction of a node's own configuration from its durable stores, and the leader's commitment is built from that configuration, so the durability of a client acknowledgement is decided by the reconstructed quorum rather than by the committed one.

comparisons.description: Five-voter case with the flag enabled: an acknowledged commit is expected to be durable on a majority of the committed configuration.
Five-voter case with the flag enabled: whether the acknowledged payload is absent from every store once the higher-term leadership has replicated over the holder.
Control: with the flag disabled the single running member of a five-voter committed configuration cannot acknowledge a commit at all.

before.description: Whether a restarted instance whose reconstruction is empty still enforces the committed configuration's voter gate when it decides whether to grant support. Thirteen in-process cases: the eleven previously exercised restart shapes plus a vote_gate_after_restart case run with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and disabled. In that case a three-peer cluster demotes one peer to a nonvoter while it keeps receiving entries, a voter follower is restarted alone, the leader is stopped so the restarted instance knows no leader, and the demoted peer's real transport delivers a real RequestVote to the restarted instance.
assumptions: Real raft instances in one process over the in-memory transports and the in-memory commit-tracking log store from the captured package; the restarted instance is reconnected to the two live peers in both directions.

The request represents the campaign of a peer whose own reconstruction still counts it as a voter, which is the mirror of the defect under audit: it carries that peer's real identity, address and last log entry, and claims a term one above the restarted instance's so that the request is not filtered by the duplicate-vote rule for a term in which the responder already voted during the cluster's initial election.

No responder state is fabricated: the request is delivered over the real transport to the real handler, and the responder's configuration, term and persisted vote are read back from its own memory and stable store.
Both peers hold the same last log entry, so the log up-to-dateness checks do not by themselves decide the request; the observation window after stopping the leader is 200 ms.
excluded: Disk-backed stores, real networks, pre-vote delivery, campaigns started by the target instance itself, and any claim about votes cast by peers other than the one delivering the request.

prefix.before: The new case builds a three-peer cluster with MakeClusterCustom(MakeClusterOpts{Peers: 3, Bootstrap: true, CommitTrackingLogs: true, Conf: inmemConfig with TrailingLogs 10 and RestoreCommittedLogs set per case}), demotes one non-leader peer to a nonvoter, applies 20 entries so both peers hold the same log, reads the responder's own configuration entry, voter count and snapshot count, stops only the responder and emits a vote_inputs CA_EVENT, then rebuilds the responder over its own stores and reconnects it in both directions to the two live peers. It stops the leader, waits 200 ms, reads the responder's reconstructed configuration and term, and sends a RequestVoteRequest built from the demoted peer's own header, identity and last log entry with a term one above, through that peer's in-memory transport to the restarted instance. It then emits a vote_grant CA_EVENT with the responder's reconstructed voter count, its log's voter count, the granted flag, the response term, the responder's terms before and after, the candidate's membership and vote status in the committed configuration, and the vote term and candidate persisted in the responder's stable store before and after the request.

responsibility.before: requestVote owns the decision to grant support, and its membership and voter gates are the only checks that bind a node's vote to the committed configuration; the reconstructed configuration is what those gates read.
responsibility.after: NewRaft owns the reconstruction of a node's own configuration from its durable stores, and the leader's commitment is built from that configuration, so the durability of a client acknowledgement is decided by the reconstructed quorum rather than by the committed one.

before.description: Vote-path case with the flag enabled: a peer that holds no vote in the configuration recorded in the responder's own log is not expected to receive the responder's vote.
Control: with the flag disabled the same request from the same peer is refused because that peer holds no vote in the responder's configuration.

Five-voter case with the flag enabled: whether the acknowledged payload is absent from every store once the higher-term leadership has replicated over the holder.
Control: with the flag disabled the single running member of a five-voter committed configuration cannot acknowledge a commit at all.

revision_reason: Adds the five-voter lost_entry_discard case with its flag-disabled control, including the extra election that puts the returning majority in a strictly higher term than the stale holder's leadership so the holder's extra entries conflict and are truncated. Replaces the comparison set with the durability, discard and acknowledgement predicates.
